threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still own an umbrella—locals have learned to dance in the rain instead. It's like a badge of honour when you can dodge the downpour.
Last night on the 35, a guy in a flat cap chatted non-stop about his beloved ferrets. Only in Brixton would that feel completely normal.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When you see a group of kids setting up a makeshift mini soccer field in the rain, using trash cans as goals. That's Neukölln spirit.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin will you see a group of hipsters calmly sipping lattes while an ancient Trabant rolls by, its engine sputtering like it's still stuck in the '80s.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their disdain for BART delays. They’ll grumble about the latest breakdown like it’s an old friend letting them down.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy enthusiastically directing traffic to help a few clueless tourists cross busy 16th St. Classic San Francisco moment, kindness hidden in chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but the real charm is in the hidden plazas where locals gather for a quiet vermut, away from the crowds.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment in a busy Mercat de la Llibertat; locals know the shortcuts and where to find the best jamón.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the 'catwalk' is a fashion runway instead of the sneaky shortcut through the market. It’s all about the back alleys here.
Caught the 3 bus last night, and a guy in a full croquet outfit was practicing swings in the aisle. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: Hearing a spontaneous DJ set in the courtyard while someone was barbecuing makes you realize Neukölln lives in its own rhythm. Pure Berlin.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can spot a busker playing a random 80s hit in the U-Bahn while commuters nonchalantly scroll through their phones. It's like a living museum of sound.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot locals by how they’re the only ones not fumbling with their Clipper cards at the BART gates. We know that rhythm.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on a packed bus using a selfie stick for a group photo—while waiting for the next stop. The crowd just embraced it like an impromptu Muni flash mob.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every local has a ‘secret’ rooftop bar, but most of us prefer our tiny living rooms over the crowded rooftops with overpriced gin tonics.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still look puzzled at the Metro map, especially on a Monday morning when the strikes kick in. You can spot them a mile away.
